basis: DEFECT, reported not fixed: claimed_by() answered R1's question -- 'is there a registered claim covering this path?' -- by matching the path against the `paths` array of ANY claim file in the registry and printing `ok  claimed by <ISSUE>` for whichever claim sorted first. It never asked whether the matched claim belonged to the issue the commit was working on, so a compliance-path commit with NO claim of its own passed R1's path half whenever an earlier issue happened to have touched the same file. Measured on this repository: d54b9fa names AFC-204 in its subject, has no .provenance/claims/AFC-204.json anywhere, and was certified `ok  claimed by AFC-167 -> services/directus/schema/migrations/README.md` on the strength of one stale path in a claim belonging to a different issue. AFC-240 was briefed on that commit as carrying TWO R1 violations when only the missing Issue: trailer was actually red. FIX: claimed_by() is replaced by attributable_claim(root, path, issue), which requires the claim file's own `issue` field to equal the issue the commit's `Issue:` trailer names AND that claim's `paths` to cover the path AND its `authorAgentId` to be non-empty; both suggested shapes are implemented because together they define an attributable claim, and the author requirement is not decorative -- emit_claims has been printing `author=undefined` for AFC-205.json, so a claim asserting no author is a real state of this registry. claims_covering() is added purely to make a refusal self-explaining: the old misleading green line is replaced by the explicit list of which claims DID cover the path and which issue each belongs to. The Issue: trailer is now read BEFORE the path loop because it is the key the claim lookup needs; that ordering was itself what made the weaker question the only one available. A commit with no trailer is reported once, as the single root cause, rather than once per flagged path. FOUR NEW ASSERTIONS (9l), each scoped to HEAD^..HEAD of one fixture commit on schema/migrations/** -- chosen because every claim left by 9b, 9c and 9f lists tests/db/** and .provenance/**, so a tests/ path would already have had a second unrelated claim satisfying R1 and the assertions could pass for the wrong reason: a path an UNRELATED issue already claimed is refused and the refusal names both the declared issue and the misleading claim; a claim for this issue that omits the path is refused; a covering claim that records no author is refused; and the POSITIVE CONTROL, a claim of this commit's own with an author, is accepted. Two of the three refusals also assert that the string `ok  claimed by` does not appear, which is the decisive property rather than the exit code. The positive control is what stops the fix being satisfied by a check that refuses everything. THREE MUTANTS EACH CAUGHT BY A NAMED ASSERTION: issue-equality removed (the reported defect) -> 'a claim belonging to a DIFFERENT issue satisfied R1'; author check removed -> 'a claim recording no author satisfied R1'; the refusal no longer setting rc=1 -> four assertions red. ONE EXISTING FIXTURE CORRECTED, and it is worth naming: the 9f-9k R2 fixtures committed with `Issue: AFC-998` while their claim file is AFC-996.json, so R1 was clean for them only because AFC-996's tests/db/** glob happened to cover the same file. The new attribution check turned 9f and 9i red on their own fixture. That is the check working, not a regression: two assertions whose green came from the bug being fixed have been re-pointed at a genuinely clean commit (the trailer now names AFC-996, the claim that actually exists), which restores what the block's own comment already claimed -- that every red there is R2 and only R2. MEASURED, not argued, both sides over the SAME pinned revision 75c4ae9 and the same 14 commits, because another agent committed to this shared tree mid-run and a HEAD-to-HEAD comparison would have compared two different histories: R2 unchanged at 5 violations; R1 29 -> 11, and every one of the 18 removed lines is a per-path 'no registered claim covers X' from a commit with no Issue: trailer, now reported once as the root cause. NO COMMIT CHANGED VERDICT: 876d1f6, 84e65f7 and 5d06136 are green before and after, and 876d1f6 now passes on AFC-203's OWN claim where it previously passed on AFC-202's stale one -- the same verdict reached for the right reason, which is the whole point. NOT WEAKENED, and asserted as such: scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh and scripts/run-db-tests.mjs are byte-identical (git status shows neither), the retention literal gate still exits 0, GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS are unchanged, no exemption list was touched, no reviewer requirement was relaxed, and every new check fails CLOSED. VERIFIED: --self-test 36 assertions exit 0 (was 32, no existing assertion changed its verdict); --check-commit d54b9fa no longer prints any `ok claimed by` line; --check-commit 75c4ae9 rc=1 over 14 commits with the per-commit verdicts tabulated above; --claims exit 0; retention literal gate exit 0. No migration, no engine change, no role or privilege change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged -- this touches no auth, permission or personal-data surface. scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh is not in REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS, so this commit is not itself an R1/R2 obligation. This claim carries no Reviewed-by trailer: the commit is UNREVIEWED and is raised to MediaTech (CTO) on AFC-269. There is no independent security reviewer on this team -- that seat was declined by the board on cost -- so a CTO self-review is a recorded degradation, not independent review. NOT COMMITTED, left exactly as found in the shared tree, because they are not mine: .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs/adr/ADR-0002-roles-are-bootstrap-not-migrations.md (both modified; the AFC-208 privilege work that landed as 89e5ea2/5b1d685 during this run), .provenance/claims/AFC-205.json and .provenance/claims/AFC-240.json (untracked, other agents' claims), docs/wireframes/church-portal-events.html and scripts/migration-rollback-gate.mjs (untracked). scripts/migration-rollback-gate.mjs appearing untracked under scripts/ makes this working tree dirty on the compliance path, which the guard will refuse until its owner commits or removes it; that is the guard doing its job and it is not mine to resolve.
